Optimal.Notes: A locked 40 fps at 40 Hz feels perfectly smooth for Subnautica's exploration pace and the medium settings keep the ocean visuals vibrant; FSR at 1024x640 recovers clarity with minimal artifacting. This is the recommended daily-driver profile for most players.

profiles.Summary: Subnautica runs well on the Steam Deck under Proton, with its modest PC requirements (GTX 550 Ti recommended) sitting comfortably within the Deck's GPU capability, allowing medium-to-high settings at native resolution with stable frame rates. The game is Steam Deck Verified and ProtonDB platinum-rated, so expect a smooth out-of-the-box experience with little to no configuration needed.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum/recommended requirements (GTX 550 Ti recommended, well within Deck capability) and the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU class. On first run, check frame rates in the Kelp Forest and Mushroom Forest biomes — the densest early-game areas — and drop to the Optimal profile if you see sustained dips below 35 fps.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at 960x600 with FSR upscaling and a tight TDP cap of 7 W keeps the battery well above 4 hours; the underwater world still looks attractive even at low settings. Expect brief loading stutters when entering new biomes regardless of settings.

KnownIssues: Some players report occasional stutters during chunk loading when exploring new underwater biomes for the first time.
The game's Unity engine can cause memory spikes in dense areas like the Lost River or Lava Zone, potentially dropping frames.
VR support is listed but not functional on Steam Deck; standard flatscreen play is unaffected.
No specific Deck-side issues reported beyond typical Proton/Unity first-launch shader compilation stutter.

MaxPerformance.Notes: At full native resolution with high settings the Deck GPU can sustain 50-60 fps in most open-water areas, though dense biomes like the Lost River may dip to the mid-40s; Motion Blur is disabled to keep the image clean at variable frame rates. Battery life is short at full TDP, so keep a charger nearby for long sessions.

Optimal.Notes: A 40 Hz refresh with a matched frame cap delivers a fluid, tear-free experience that suits the slow-paced exploration gameplay. FSR at this render resolution recovers most visual clarity on the OLED screen.

profiles.Summary: Subnautica runs well on the Steam Deck, meeting the recommended specs comfortably with the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU and Zen 2 CPU. The game is Steam Deck Verified with a strong platinum ProtonDB rating, indicating a smooth out-of-the-box experience with minimal issues.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum/recommended specs (the Deck's GPU sits comfortably above the minimum and near the recommended tier) and the game's Verified status. On first run, check frame rate in a large open biome like the Safe Shallows and adjust Quality preset up or down accordingly.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at 960x600 with FSR upscaling keeps TDP low and extends battery significantly. The underwater environments still look atmospheric at these settings due to the game's art direction.

KnownIssues: Occasional stuttering or hitching when new chunks of the ocean load in (streaming open-world nature of the game)
Long initial shader compilation on first launch may cause temporary freezes
VR support listed but not applicable on Deck
Some users report memory pressure in late-game areas with many base modules built

MaxPerformance.Notes: Native 1280x800 at high settings is achievable in most areas, but expect dips toward 40-45 fps in dense coral reefs or large base areas; dropping Quality to 'Good' can stabilize these spots. Motion Blur is disabled as it adds GPU cost with little benefit on a small screen.
